sub1: A 24-line link supplied as a grid and assessed here — fifteen turns, cover weeks perfectly spaced, and two gates it does not clear

sub3: What this design keeps of today, and the two places it does not pay the contract or the rest rule
openQuestions: It does not clear two gates, and both are refusals rather than findings. 1 · One rest under 12 hours: line 7's Saturday 12:00–20:00 runs into line 8's Sunday 07:15–15:45, leaving 11h15. A minimum rest is a condition of a design being runnable, so the workspace generator repairs this shape or refuses it — it is the same complaint that made rest a gate rather than a report. 2 · Sixty minutes over contract: Monday to Saturday totals 42,060 minutes where 20 working lines × 35h is 42,000. The contract is an equality, not a floor: a permanent surplus commits the rotation to an hour of overtime nobody declared. One duty needs to be an hour shorter, or the cover-week count has to move. What it gets right that the others do not: the cover weeks are perfectly even (6, 6, 6, 6), the turn table is the shortest of any proposal at fifteen times, and the week-to-week step is 2h16 against Weekday Lates' 4h43.
